BIS: "mahimong maghatag og mas mapuslanon nga mga pagsabog" = more USEFUL/beneficial eruptions. `mapuslanon` means useful/advantageous everywhere else in this corpus (138 cards). Nothing else in the card says explosive or dangerous, so a Cebuano-only reader learns the opposite of the hazard point the card exists to make. Correct: "mas kusog/mabungrot nga pagsabog".

title_en "Sharp Obsidian Glass" -> title_bis "Obsidian nga Matarong". `matarong` = righteous/upright (moral), never sharp; Cebuano for sharp is `hait` — which this card's OWN body uses ("Grabe ka hait kini"), so the title is the outlier. Systematic in the corpus: ffct-13345 "Fovea Matarong" and ffct-02597 "Matarong nga Ngipon sa Karniboro" repeat the same swap.

Safety card. EN "DUCK down" is glossed in BIS as "DUCK (magtaob)". In Cebuano `taob` is the rising/high TIDE (96 cards in this corpus use it that way: "pagtaob ug paghunas sa dagat") — it is the Tagalog false friend of *taob* (face-down/overturned). The gloss is the only explanation of the action and points up, not down; correct is `duko` / `moduko`.

EN "Soft parts decay too quickly to become fossils" -> BIS "Paspas ra mabulok ang humok nga bahin". `bulok` = COLOUR in Cebuano (this corpus: "mabulokon nga bulak", "pinakabulokon nga balhibo", "mabulokon ang taklobo"); decay is `madunot`, used in 234 other cards. The causal clause that answers the card's own question is destroyed (reads "the soft part quickly becomes coloured"); the same sentence also uses Tagalog `matagas` for hard instead of `gahi`.

EN hedges twice: "one of the world's biggest geothermal power plants" / "MakBan ... is one of the largest geothermal complexes in the Philippines and the world". The Cebuano drops the hedge in BOTH places: the question becomes "Asa ang labing dagkong geothermal complex sa kalibutan?" (where is the world's LARGEST) and the answer is flatly "Ang MakBan sa Laguna ug Batangas, Pilipinas!" — the clause "usa sa labing dagko" appears nowhere. A Cebuano-only child learns MakBan is the single largest geothermal complex on Earth, which is false and unrecoverable from the card. Same defect class as gold row ffct-17976 (quantifier dropped -> class-wide claim).

Cave-safety card. EN: "always wear a helmet, bring light, and go with a guide". BIS: "kanunay og sumbrera ug dala ang suga" — sumbrera is a HAT, not a helmet, and nothing else in the card mentions head protection. Corpus cross-check is decisive: of 26 cards whose English says "helmet", 25 keep the word "helmet" in the Cebuano; ffct-33006 is the only "sumbrera" in all 49,156 cards. A child is told a hat is the gear for entering a cave.

The whole point of a binary cycle is that the secondary fluid BOILS at a low temperature. EN: "The isobutane boils easily and spins the turbine". BIS: "Sayon mosinaw ang isobutane ug mopalikid sa turbine" — sinaw is shine/shiny (corpus: masinaw nga dahon, sinaw nga perlas), never boil; the corpus renders "boil" as mobukal/nagbukal in 144 cards. No other sentence in the card says bukal or singaw, so the mechanism is gone: the child reads that isobutane "shines easily" and cannot say why a cooler geothermal fluid can still drive the turbine.

title_bis "EGS nga Lawom nga Buto" vs title_en "Enhanced Geothermal Systems". In this corpus standalone "buto" is BONE (46 cards: buto sa hita, nabaling buto) and in verb form an explosion (pagbuto sa bulkan) — neither is a drilled well. The card's own body proves the intended word: "Nagbutas ang mga inhinyero og lawom" (butas = hole). So the title is the outlier and reads as "EGS, the Deep Bone/Deep Blast", teaching a child scanning titles that EGS is an underground explosion rather than deep drilling. Same shape as gold row ffct-10181 (agta vs agup-op in the title).

title_bis "Yuta nga Nituyo sa Adlaw" for title_en "Earth Orbits the Sun". Cebuano "tuyo/nituyo" is purpose / did-on-purpose (corpus: gituyo sa buwaya ang pagtulon og bato, gituyo nimo nga usbon) and "nituyo" appears in exactly zero other cards; orbit/spin is tuyok (552 cards), which this card's own body uses correctly ("nagtuyok sa Adlaw"). The title of a heliocentrism card therefore states no orbital relation at all — it reads "Earth that intended the Sun".

title_bis "Singaw nga Tuyo Turbine" for title_en "Steam Spins the Turbine". "Tuyo" in Cebuano is purpose, or dried fish (corpus: bulad/tuyo, gituyo = on purpose) — never spin, which is tuyok/palikid; the body itself says "mopalikid sa turbine blades" correctly. The title as shipped names a different thing (dried/intentional steam) and drops the spin relationship the card exists to teach. Same writer-level error as ffct-33013 above, so it is worth grepping title_bis corpus-wide for tuyo-where-tuyok-is-meant.

EN: "Animals in the Philippine Trench survive extreme water pressure over 1,100 times the surface!" BIS: "makabuhi sa grabe ka taas nga presyon sa tubig" — the 1,100x figure is simply absent (it is the only en/bis digit mismatch in the batch that is not an idiomatic rewrite). The card's one quantitative fact is gone, so a child reading only the Cebuano cannot say how much pressure the trench animals withstand. Lowest-confidence of the seven: the qualitative claim (extreme pressure, special adaptations) does survive.

Body reverses the Earth-Sun relationship that the whole card rests on. EN: "since Earth also moves around the Sun, the Moon must travel a bit farther". BIS: "apan nagdala usab ang Yuta sa Adlaw, kaya kinahanglan pa og dugang ang Moon" — 'nagdala ... sa Adlaw' = the EARTH CARRIES/BRINGS THE SUN, not that Earth orbits the Sun (naglibot sa Adlaw). A child reading only the Cebuano gets a false relation (Earth carrying the Sun) and cannot recover the actual reason the synodic period (29.5 d) exceeds the sidereal one (27.3 d); nothing else in the card restores it.

title_bis "Uma nga Red Giant" for title_en "Sun's Red Giant Future". 'Uma' in Cebuano is a FARM / farmland — it is used with exactly that meaning elsewhere in this same batch (ffct-33102: "aron himoong umahan"). The intended word is 'umaabot' (future/coming); truncated to 'Uma' the title names a different thing entirely (a farm that is a red giant) and the word 'uma' never reappears in the body to be corrected. The body also weakens the time direction: "Mga 5 bilyong tuig na karon" for "in about 5 billion years" (the 'ago' form used in this corpus is "na ang milabay", cf. ffct-33134), so the title is the only place 'future' was supposed to live.

title_bis "Polaris nga Amihan" for "Polaris the North Star". In Cebuano 'amihan' is the NORTHEAST MONSOON / north wind — the same batch uses it that way as a standalone title (ffct-33103 title_bis "Amihan" = "Northeast Monsoon"). North as a direction is 'amihanan'; a star is 'bituon'. The title therefore names a wind, not a star, and the body never supplies any Cebuano rendering to correct it (it only carries the English strings "North Star" and "north pole").

Number changed by two orders of magnitude. EN: "formed from the weathering of ultramafic rocks like peridotite over millions of years". BIS: "sulod sa gatusan ka milyon ka tuig" = over HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS of years. Not a spelled-out-digit difference — the magnitude itself is different, and nothing in the Cebuano card restores the correct figure, so a child ends up with a wrong number for how long the Surigao nickel/iron laterite took to form.

EN: "regolith — crushed rock and dust with sharp edges". BIS: "crushed rock ug abug nga adunay MATALINGHAGA nga mga kilid" — 'matalinghaga' means figurative/metaphorical/obscure, not sharp ('hait'). The sharpness is the card's distinguishing fact about regolith and it appears nowhere else in the Cebuano; the closing clause that would imply it is also broken ("walay hangin o tubig nga MIPAKIN" — 'mipakin' is not a word; 'smoothed' = mipahamis), so a child cannot recover why lunar dust is sharp/unweathered.

Body: "adunay igo nga gravity aron manghikog (hydrostatic equilibrium)". English is "have enough gravity to be round". "Manghikog" in Cebuano means TO COMMIT SUICIDE / hang oneself — not "to become round" (lingin/bilog). The card never says round anywhere; the only remaining hint is the untranslated English jargon "hydrostatic equilibrium", which a grade-5 reader cannot decode. So rule 2 of the IAU planet definition is unrecoverable from the Cebuano, and the sentence additionally reads as self-harm content in a children's card.

title_bis "Mga Labay sa Jupiter" for "Jupiter's Bands". Cebuano "labay" = to throw / to pass by (Tagalog: a skein of yarn) — it is not a stripe or band. The card's OWN body uses the correct word: "Ang makulay nga guhit sa Jupiter" — strong evidence the title is the outlier, and the title as a standalone label names a different thing.

title_bis "Ngano Moulaw" for "Why It Rains". "Ulaw" is a real Cebuano word meaning shame/shyness (maulaw = to be embarrassed); rain is "ulan". The body has the correct form twice ("Nganong moulan?" / "Moulan kung..."), so the title is the single wrong word and reads as "Why be ashamed".

title_bis "Pagtapak sa Black Hole" for "How Black Holes Form". Cebuano "tapak" = to step on / to patch, not to form; the card's own body uses the right word ("Unsaon pagporma sa mga black hole?"). As a standalone title it names a different action (stepping on a black hole) than the English.

The card asks "unsay nahitabo sa iyang biyahe?" and answers "nagkaproblema sa dihang nagsabog sa gawas ang iyang spacesuit". "Sabog" in Cebuano = to scatter / blow apart, so the Cebuano says Leonov's spacesuit BURST APART, while the English says it ballooned (inflated, miburot/mihubag) outward. The suit did not rupture, and nothing else in the card restores the inflation fact — the child answers the card's own question with a false event.

title_bis reads "Plato Ika-siyam Bago 2006" — the card is about PLUTO, but the Cebuano title names "Plato", which in this very corpus is the word for a tectonic/dinner PLATE (12 other bis titles: "Lithosphere Plato", "Subduction Plato", "Pagduso sa mga Plato", "Ceramic sa Plato ug Tasa"). Provable bis-only corruption: the tl title of the same card is correct ("Pluto, Ika-siyam Bago 2006") and the card's own Cebuano body says "Pluto" twice, so the title is the outlier. A child browsing the feed by title is told a plate was the ninth planet before 2006; the fact is only recoverable after opening the card.

title_en "Charon, Half of Pluto" -> title_bis "Charon, Kalimot sa Pluto". "Kalimot" is forgetting/forgetfulness (root limot), not "half" (katunga). The card's OWN body uses the correct word ("Ang Charon mga katunga sa gidak-on sa Pluto"), so the title is the outlier: it names a different thing and states nothing about size.

title_en "Length of a Lunar Day" -> title_bis "Gabii sa Lunar Day". "Gabii" is NIGHT, not length/duration (gidugayon/kadugayon). The body asks and answers duration correctly ("Unsa kadugay... molungtad og mga 24 ka oras ug 50 ka minuto"), so the title alone asserts a different thing - a child scanning titles reads "night of a lunar day", which is a distinct (and wrong) concept from the 24h50m cycle length.

title_en "Voyager 1 Launch" -> title_bis "Paglusad: Voyager 1". Cebuano "lusad" = to go down / alight / disembark - the opposite direction from a launch, which is "lunsad". The card's own body uses the correct form twice ("Kanus-a gilunsad...", "gilunsad sa kalawakan sa tuig 1977"), confirming the title is the outlier and a direction reversal, not a regional variant.

title_en "Spring Tide Isn't Spring" -> title_bis "Spring Tide Dili Tag". The title is cut off mid-word: "Dili Tag" denies nothing - "Tag" is a dangling prefix (tag-init / tag-ulan / tingpamulak). The body names the season correctly ("Bahin ba sa tingpamulak...", "walay kalambigitan sa tingpamulak"), so the title dropped the very term the card exists to deny.
